There are four versions of the adults and you get two of each version, giving a total of eight Adults.

By far the most numerous of the Intruders are the Adults. These are the Intruders that the crew members are most likely to encounter. Once again, they can have two to six wounds depending upon which card is drawn when they are injured. Each time you injure an Intruder you draw a card to determine how many wounds it has so it can vary in a single turn if you injure it multiple times. Rolling the combat dice you have a 3 in 6 chance of wounding them.

There are four versions of the adults and you get two of each version, giving a total of eight Adults. The two standing Intruders have bits of debris sculpted on their bases with pieces fixed to their legs and hands to add strength to their sculpts, otherwise they might snap at their ankles. It is a wise decision that the sculptors made.

These are three Intruders you least want to encounter. Two Breeders stand on either side of the mighty Queen. When you injure one of these figures you draw two cards to determine how many wounds it has. This gives them a range of four to twelve wounds depending upon which cards are drawn.

# Nemesis: Retaliation Image

Setup & Reference Utility

Configure the drop — boosters, mode, alien race and squad size — for exact setup steps, a full rules reference with the official FAQ v1.2 rulings applied, and a search of every rulebook.

Fourteen rounds. One Lander. Good luck, marine.

## Mission Loadout

Select what's on the table. Every step and ruling below adapts to your choices.

Sets in play — the Insider works only with the base game and Character boosters

Retaliation Base game Contractors Characters Support Squad Characters Insider Story Sangrevores Alt. race Neoflesh Cult Alt. race Xyrians 3rd faction

Game mode

Standard Semi-cooperative. Private and Mission Objectives, one shared Mission Task. 2-5 players.Solo / Co-op Fully cooperative or alone. One Solo/Coop Mission Task per Character — all must be fulfilled.

Alien race — Sangrevores and Neoflesh Cult replace the Primebloods

Primebloods The classic hive: Larvae, Adults, Drones and the Queen.Sangrevores Requires the Sangrevores expansion Neoflesh Cult Requires the Neoflesh Cult expansion
#### Corridors

  * Capacity: 6 Intruders (the Queen counts as 4) or a Noise marker — a Corridor with only a Noise marker still counts as empty; an Intruder entering discards the marker.
  * Reinforce (via Actions, empty Corridors only — no Intruders; never through a Closed Door): discard its Noise marker, if any, and flip the Corridor to its “0” side. Noise rolls can't place markers there (Intruders can still move into it; Hibernatorium Corridors can't be Reinforced).

Retaliation p.21-25, 32 · FAQ v1.2 p.2

Combat & Intruder Health

Hits work differently by location: in a Corridor, each Hit kills 1 Adult outright (Drones need 2 at once; leftover Hit markers never persist there); in a Room, Hits accumulate as Universal markers by the model.

#### Shoot (1 card)

  1. Pick a working, loaded Ranged Weapon and an Intruder in your Room.
  2. Deal 1 Hit, then roll the Shoot die: skull = it dies; 2-5 = it dies if the roll ≤ its total Hits; ammo symbol = spend 1 Ammo (flip full → half, discard half). Shooting otherwise costs no Ammo!

Retaliation p.23, 37-40 · FAQ v1.2 p.2-3

The Robot

  * One of 6 Robot cards is in play, face down on the Section “A” border piece; it's revealed when any Room first connects to the Hibernatorium. The model starts in the Hibernatorium.
  * Activate the Robot (1 card): locally in its Room, or remotely from any Room with a Computer for 1 extra card (a Data token waives the extra card). Each Robot card has a unique effect.
  * Intruders completely ignore it. It never moves on its own, moves Room-to-Room via player Actions, can't pass Closed Doors or Unexplored Corridors, and makes no Noise rolls (exception: the Exploration Robot may Explore a new Room, and then it can make a Noise roll).
  * It carries 1 Ammo + 1 Oxygen token; Characters in its Room can use and swap its Tactical Gear.
  * A Malfunction marker blanks its card (Gear still usable; effects merely requiring a Robot still work; FAQ: Robot-related Events still resolve).

Retaliation p.8, 23, 37 · FAQ v1.2 p.3

Key FAQ Rulings (v1.2)

  * Fire At Will (Officer): the Officer picks their Room or a neighboring one; each Character in Turn order Bursts at a Corridor the Officer chooses (it can differ per Character), with their choice of Weapon.

    [Sunday February 08 2026] [+1 votes]
    The odds are better than in og.
    And certain characters are better for dealing with intruders in rooms.
    Some characters have rerolls.
    Some characters deal 2 damage instead of 1, so an intruder kill is guaranteed in 3 shots.
    Some characters have double the chance for a crit.
    Some characters can easily repel intruders into corridors for easy kills.
    And don’t forget about support item draft, the items can help you deal with the weakness of your character.
    Shooting also doesn’t cost ammo unless you toll the ammo symbol.

      [Thursday February 12 2026] [+1 votes]
      Well not guaranteed kill in 3 shots, you can theoretically roll infinite ammo symbol and never get the kill. Super unlikely however, I've seen max 2 in a row.

        [Thursday February 12 2026] [+1 votes]
        Yea 7/8 chance to kill after tree shots.
Anytime you pull an event card it instructs you to move intruders in a relevant corridor orientation - it's almost always followed by "then ALL intruders in rooms move." which puts them back in corridors. Unless they're in combat, intruders are almost never hanging out in rooms.
Grenades are powerful, they clear corridors. But they work best when you follow the intruder movement rules!
When intruders enter a player-occupied room from a corridor, only one intruder (the largest) enters the room.
Your corridors have a lot of connections - a rule a lot of people miss is that when exploring you never place corridors to already explored rooms. More corridors means more noise, which means more intruders.
It also sounds like you're possibly doing shooting wrong. Queen health works the same as an adult intruder, always apply damage when you shoot and see if you roll under whatever her damage is on the tracker.
There's also rules people mess up because they were rules in nemesis, and they're not rules anymore. The rulebook has lots of things that it won't tell you "this is no longer a rule" and that trips a lot of people up who played the first two games.
